question: What is the primary physical sign associated with neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Yellowish discoloration of the skin and sclera
options.B: Severe pallor of the mucous membranes
options.C: Generalized petechial rashes on the trunk
options.D: Diffuse bluish cyanosis of the extremities

explanation: Neonatal jaundice is characterized by hyperbilirubinemia, which visibly presents as a yellow tint to the skin and sclera. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: In which anatomical area does the cephalocaudal progression of neonatal jaundice typically begin?
explanation: Jaundice spreads in a cephalocaudal direction, meaning it becomes visible on the face and head first before moving down to the trunk and limbs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which enzyme is primarily responsible for converting unconjugated bilirubin into conjugated bilirubin in the liver?
explanation: Glucuronyl transferase facilitates the conjugation process, making lipid-soluble bilirubin water-soluble for excretion. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: Why is unconjugated bilirubin considered potentially hazardous to the central nervous system?

options.A: It precipitates directly within renal tubular cells
options.B: It actively binds to cerebral calcium channels
options.C: It is lipid-soluble and can cross the blood-brain barrier
options.D: It stimulates excessive production of cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin dissolves in lipids, allowing it to penetrate neural tissues and cause neurotoxicity when levels are extremely high. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: What is a defining characteristic of pathological jaundice compared to physiological jaundice?

options.A: Spontaneous resolution by the fifth day without treatment
options.B: Absence of any elevation in conjugated bilirubin fractions
options.C: Onset within the first twenty-four hours of life
options.D: Peak serum levels occurring at the end of the second week

explanation: Any jaundice appearing in the first twenty-four hours is considered pathological and requires urgent investigation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: A term newborn is forty-eight hours old and has a mild yellow tint to the face that is steadily declining. What process best explains this clinical picture?

options.A: Acute bilirubin encephalopathy secondary to sepsis
options.B: Congenital biliary atresia requiring surgical correction
options.C: Severe hemolytic disease from blood group incompatibility
options.D: Normal physiological adaptation to extrauterine life

explanation: Appearing after twenty-four hours with a self-limiting course is typical of physiological jaundice resulting from immature hepatic pathways. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: Which inherited enzyme deficiency is particularly prevalent in Nigeria and frequently triggers severe neonatal hemolysis?
explanation: G6PD deficiency is common across sub-Saharan Africa and makes red blood cells prone to rapid destruction when exposed to oxidative triggers. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: A nursing mother in a postpartum ward in Lagos mentions placing traditional camphor balls in her baby's wardrobe. Why is this practice dangerous for a newborn?

options.A: It alters skin pigmentation, mimicking true pathological jaundice
options.B: It directly inactivates hepatic glucuronyl transferase enzymes
options.C: It causes immediate mechanical blockage of the bile canaliculi
options.D: It can precipitate acute hemolysis in infants with undiagnosed G6PD deficiency

explanation: Camphor vapors act as strong oxidative stressors that can induce massive red blood cell breakdown in G6PD-deficient neonates. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: What bedside technique helps nurses accurately visualize jaundice beneath the skin?

options.A: Digital blanching over a bony prominence
options.C: Applying cold packs to induce localized pallor
options.D: Pinching a fold of abdominal skin firmly

explanation: Pressing the skin against a bone forces blood away temporarily, making the underlying yellow bilirubin tint much easier to observe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: Why is examination of the sclera particularly important when assessing newborn infants with dark skin pigmentation?

options.A: Scleral blood vessels dilate instantly in response to elevated serum lipids
options.B: Conjunctival membranes are immune to physiological color changes
options.C: Bilirubin deposits exclusively in ocular tissues prior to dermal layers
options.D: Melanin pigmentation in the skin can obscure the true yellowish hue

explanation: Dermal melanin can hide mild to moderate skin jaundice, making the sclera a more reliable site for early visual detection. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: What laboratory test provides the definitive value used to guide treatment decisions for neonatal jaundice?
explanation: Serum Total Bilirubin measurement gives the exact quantitative concentration needed to compare against clinical treatment nomograms. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: Why is a Packed Cell Volume (PCV) routinely ordered alongside bilirubin levels in infants with early jaundice?

options.A: To screen for concurrent anemia resulting from red blood cell breakdown
options.B: To rule out primary bone marrow failure syndromes
options.C: To calculate the exact rate of hepatic glycogen depletion
options.D: To determine whether the infant requires immediate intravenous hydration

explanation: Hemolytic processes destroy red blood cells rapidly, leading to both high bilirubin and a significantly reduced PCV. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which phototherapy reduces serum bilirubin levels?

options.A: Destroying circulating maternal antibodies within the portal vein
options.B: Accelerating renal glomerular filtration rate through diuresis
options.C: Stimulating the immediate synthesis of hepatic glucuronyl transferase
options.D: Converting unconjugated bilirubin into water-soluble photoisomers

explanation: Light energy alters the structure of bilirubin molecules into forms that dissolve easily in water and leave the body via bile and urine. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: Which nursing intervention is essential during the administration of conventional phototherapy to a newborn?

options.A: Placing the incubator directly under direct sunlight near a ward window
options.B: Wrapping the infant tightly in heavy blankets to prevent shivering
options.C: Administering oral castor oil to speed up meconium elimination
options.D: Applying opaque eye covers to prevent retinal injury from the light source

explanation: Intense phototherapy lights can damage a newborn's developing retina, making protective eye shielding a mandatory nursing safety measure. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: What term describes the permanent chronic neurological condition caused by toxic bilirubin deposits in brain tissues?
explanation: Kernicterus is the irreversible neurological syndrome resulting from severe bilirubin deposition in the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h8)

question: Which clinical signs are most characteristic of early acute bilirubin encephalopathy in a newborn?

options.A: Lethargy, poor feeding, and a high-pitched cry
options.B: Flaccid paralysis and absent deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Rapid tachypnea and marked intercostal retractions

explanation: Early neurotoxicity presents with subtle behavioral alterations such as extreme lethargy, reluctance to feed, and a characteristic high-pitched cry. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h8)

question: What is an important component of nursing care for a breastfeeding mother whose baby is undergoing continuous phototherapy?

options.A: Instructing her to remain outside the ward to prevent phototherapy equipment interference
options.B: Encouraging her to administer plain sterile water feeds between nursing sessions
options.C: Advising her to cease breastfeeding entirely until treatment concludes
options.D: Assisting her to express breast milk and supporting regular feeding intervals

explanation: Frequent feeding promotes gut motility and helps eliminate bilirubin, so supporting lactation and expressed milk feeds is vital. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h9)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate topic for parental discharge education regarding neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Recognizing signs of lethargy and poor waking responses
options.B: Ensuring frequent and effective infant feeding routines at home
options.C: Using traditional camphor balls in baby clothes to ward off infections
options.D: Monitoring for recurrence of yellow discoloration on the skin and eyes

explanation: Camphor is dangerous because it triggers severe hemolysis in G6PD-deficient infants and must be actively discouraged. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h9)
